title: When you land
body:
Lisbon Humberto Delgado Airport (LIS) sits inside the city — no long transfer. Take the Metro red line (Aeroporto–Saldanha, ≈20 min) into the center; buy a Navegante card (€0.50) plus fare at the station machine before boarding. A taxi or rideshare runs ≈€10–15 including the airport luggage fee.

The Aerobus airport shuttle some older guides mention was discontinued in 2022 — don't look for it.
checklist: Buy a Navegante card (€0.50) at an airport Metro machine, then load a single fare (€1.92) or top up for zapping (€1.72/ride)
Confirm your first night's lodging address before you land — Lisbon's Alfama/Baixa streets are narrow and easy to mistype into a taxi app

title: Local essentials
body:
Emergency number: 112 (police/fire/ambulance, free, 24/7). Tap water is safe throughout Portugal. Tipping ~5–10% in restaurants is customary but not required — nobody will chase you down for skipping it.

The bread, olives or cheese a waiter sets down without being asked (couvert) is a real, legal charge if you eat it — but Portuguese consumer law says you're never obliged to pay for anything you didn't order, and you can hand it back at no charge. Restaurants must display the couvert price; ask if it isn't shown.

title: Entry & documents
body: US passports enter Portugal visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day Schengen window. Keep your passport valid at least 3 months past your Apr 19 departure. No ETIAS authorisation is required yet — the EU pushed its target launch past Q4 2026 with no new date confirmed, so this is worth a last look before you fly (see the masthead re-check list).
checklist: Passport valid at least 3 months beyond Apr 19, 2027
Re-check ETIAS status closer to departure — travel-europe.europa.eu/etias_en

title: Phone & data
body: The EU's 'Roam Like at Home' rules cover EU/EEA residents only — a US phone plan is NOT included, so check your carrier's own international pass before you fly (AT&T/Verizon-style day-passes run roughly $10–12/day; some T-Mobile plans include basic reduced-speed data). A local prepaid SIM or eSIM from MEO or Vodafone Portugal, available at airport kiosks, is usually cheaper for a 9-day trip if your carrier doesn't already cover Europe.

title: Booking checklist
body: Start at the top — these set your dates and are the ones most likely to sell out.
checklist: Flights, round trip — TAP Air Portugal flies EWR direct to both Lisbon (LIS) and Porto (OPO), so an open-jaw (into LIS, home from OPO) skips backtracking
Accommodation — Lisbon (5 nights) and Porto (4 nights)
Pena Palace timed-entry ticket (mandatory for the interior) — book once the Sintra day (Apr 13) is fixed: bilheteira.parquesdesintra.pt
Belém Tower ticket — book ahead; the tower reopened May 2026 with a new ~900-visitor/day cap after a year of restoration
Livraria Lello ticket — books up, especially midday: tickets.livrarialello.pt
Lisbon–Porto Alfa Pendular train (Apr 15) — book at cp.pt; exact fare isn't independently confirmable against a live fetch, budget ≈€25–35pp 2nd class
Confirm your phone plan's Europe roaming or order a local eSIM

title: Public holidays & closures
note: No Portuguese national holiday falls inside Apr 10–19, 2027 — Good Friday (Mar 26) and Easter Sunday (Mar 28) land before you arrive, and Freedom Day (Apr 25) falls 6 days after you leave. Lisbon's Santo António (Jun 13) and Porto's São João (Jun 24) are also well outside your dates.
